transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I suppose I'm here because of the historical society project. I just... I took it on like I could run the entire fundraiser all by myself. I started drawing up all these new quilt designs, which, you know, quilting is something my grandmother actually taught me when I was a little girl. She had this beautiful old Singer sewing machine, one of the heavy cast-iron ones with the foot pedal? I actually saw one exactly like it at the antique mall out on Route 9 the other day. The man running the shop wanted way too much for it, though, and he was quite rude when I pointed out a scratch on the wood cabinet. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, the project. Right, so I was calling all the volunteers, making these incredibly detailed schedules for everyone, and I ended up promising the board all these deadlines I couldn't possibly meet. I just felt like I could do it all, but then... well, the antique mall also had these lovely vintage pearl buttons I really should have bought for a different project, but... I guess the fundraiser just got a bit out of hand, according to my family.
Over the past week or so, have you noticed you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy the next day?

Well, for a while there, yes. I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, and I'd pop right out of bed before the sun was even up, just completely ready to start sewing or calling the caterers for the fundraiser. Which, speaking of caterers, I found this wonderful local woman who does these little miniature quiches. They are just darling, and she uses real gruyere cheese, not the cheap stuff. My sister makes a good quiche, but she always burns the crust just a little bit, you know? She insists it's "caramelized," but I know burnt when I taste it. 

But, um, lately... no. Now it's the opposite. I either lie awake for hours just worrying about all those deadlines I missed, or I sleep until noon and I still feel completely worn out. It's like someone pulled the plug on my battery. I did buy a new mattress pad thinking that might help, one of those memory foam ones they advertise on television? The box it came in was incredibly heavy, the delivery man practically dropped it on my porch... but no, it hasn't helped the sleep at all.

During this low period, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, or had any unusual beliefs—like feeling you've done something terrible or that people are out to get you?

Hearing voices? Oh, heavens no. My hearing is perfectly fine, though my late husband used to joke I had selective hearing whenever his football games were on. He was a die-hard Packers fan, had this awful green and yellow foam hat he'd wear on Sundays. I tried to hide it in the hall closet once, right behind the winter coats, but he found it anyway... 

But, what was I saying? Oh, feeling like I've done something terrible. Yes. That part is true. I just sit there and keep going over every single late order, and every sharp thing I said to the volunteers. I really shouldn't have snapped at them, especially not at Brenda. Brenda makes the best potato salad for the church potlucks, she puts just a little bit of fresh dill in it. I tried growing dill in my herb garden last year, but the rabbits got to it before I could harvest a single sprig. They are such a nuisance, they ate all my hostas too. 

But... yes, the guilt is just awful. I just keep telling myself that I completely let the church down, and the historical society, and basically this whole town. It just eats away at me, feeling like I ruined everything for everyone.
During this low period, have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself or that you'd be better off not being alive?

Well, I... I certainly don't have any sort of plan to hurt myself, nothing like that. I couldn't do that to my family. Though, speaking of family, my daughter just got a new puppy, a little golden retriever mix, and he is just the sweetest thing. She brought him over yesterday, but he tracked mud all over my front rug. It's one of those braided rugs, the kind that are just impossible to get clean once the dirt gets ground into the fibers. I tried using that spot cleaner they sell at the hardware store, the one with the orange scent? It smells entirely too strong, gave me a bit of a headache, honestly. 

But... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the... the thoughts. It's just... sometimes, I catch myself thinking that it would just be so much easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. Then nobody would have to deal with the mess I've made of everything. The historical society wouldn't have to scramble to fix my mistakes, and my family wouldn't have to worry about me. It just feels like I'm such a burden to everyone right now.
